definition.value: A multi-die accelerator is a design approach in which an AI accelerator, presented as one device, is built from more than one die assembled in one package. The Atlas calls it multi-die; 'chiplet' is used only where a source uses it.
A multi-die package is the packaging of two or more dies in one package so that they work as one functional subsystem. The Atlas calls it multi-die; 'chiplet' is used only where a source uses it.
Electronic design automation (EDA) is the class of software used to design chips. A vendor's EDA tool is a product, not this record.

Cloud computing is a service model: on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources, rapidly provisioned and released with minimal management effort, as NIST defines it. A provider's cloud service is a product, not this record.
